messages:
anja: heads-up — after yesterday's queue tweak i see a perf regression on a subset of requests. p95 latency for short prompts jumped ~20% for the low-decode-rate cohort. digging into batch formation

michael: which cohort exactly? prompt length bucket or decode-rate bucket?

anja: decode-rate bucket. the classifier is sending a lot of short prompts (<=40 tokens) that decode at ~15 tok/s into the same pool as slow decoders (~5 tok/s). when the slow ones get in, they starve the fast ones and the batching timer keeps stretching.

sam: hmm. can you paste the profiler slice? curious about queue wait vs decode time.

anja: quick snippet from the trace (stripped):
```
queue_wait_ms: p50=6, p95=82
batch_size_tokens: avg=220
decode_time_ms_per_token: cohort_fast=12, cohort_slow=200
kv_cache_hit_rate: fast=0.92, slow=0.64
```

anja: note the big decode delta and the lower KV hit for the slow cohort — could be cache eviction or big prompts earlier.

rachel: low kv hit on slow cohort suggests either different prompt shape or cache keys missing. did we evict more earlier because of a larger token budget setting?

michael: last rollout bumped the token_budget_target from 1024 -> 2048 for a burstier workload. that helps long chat flows, but increases KV pressure and batch token totals. might explain the higher avg batch tokens.

sam: quick experiment idea: split the decode-rate classifier into two explicit queues: fast_decoders (<25 tok/s) and normal. also add a hard max wait for fast_decoders (e.g., 12ms) to avoid being held by slow ones.

anja: yeah — my local probe: switched to two pools + token_budget_target back to 1200 for the normal pool. results across 1m sample: p50 unchanged, p95 for fast cohort improved from 220ms -> 175ms, overall cost +1.2% but tail better.

michael: good. what about kernel selection? are slow decoders sometimes forcing fallback to a slower kernel causing the gap?

anja: i checked — kernel selection stayed stable for the model family. the slow cohort stalls are mostly due to long per-token decode and lower KV hit, not kernel fallback.

rachel: could also be that slow cohort uses longer context so attention kernels blow up mem and cause GC-like pauses. do we have trace of per-step allocation?

sam: not in that probe. i can run an allocation profile. but we should also consider a percentile-based token_budget instead of global target. e.g., set target to 90th pct of recent token distribution per-cohort. that reduces eviction noise.

michael: +1 to pct-based. also add a min_batch_tokens cap for fast queue (so tiny requests don't get grouped into huge token batches). e.g., min_batch_tokens=32, max_wait_ms=12.

anja: note on config we should avoid oscillation: when a cohort flips buckets frequently, we end up thrashing. suggest adding a 30s hysteresis on classifier assignment or a stability window.

jorge: agree on hysteresis. also from infra side we'll add a perf guard in the rollout: if fast cohort p95 regresses >10% for 5m, auto-roll back. deploy-bot will handle the signal.

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-11-02T08:12Z: started canary to 10% of cluster (config: fast_queue_wait_ms=12, min_batch_tokens=32, token_budget_pct=90)

sam: i ran a 15m canary in staging. notes: KV hit stabilized (+3.5pp), fast p95 down 18%, slow cohort p95 up 4% (acceptable). raw numbers: fast p95 175ms -> 143ms in staging canary.

anja: thanks. i'll prepare an A/B evaluation harness to run for 3h across production traffic slices. include metrics: p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, kv-hit, batch_tokens distribution, and decode-rate histogram.

michael: put a short query in console to show cohort assignment rate and churn: helpful to validate hysteresis.

rachel: small followup — for KV we should also log representative prompt hashes for slow cohort to see if it's different template space (privacy-safe sampling).

anja: agreed. will add safe-sample. plan: run canary 3h -> evaluate -> promote if fast p95 improved and slow p95 regression <=5%.

jorge: I'll keep the rollback ready and watch infra alarms. thanks all. :thumbsup:
